extracted.intended_audience: immigration applicants, sponsors, attorneys and representatives, public commenters, and agency/OMB reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for commenting on and understanding DHS/USCIS information collection instruments (Forms I-693, I-864 series, I-944, I-912, I-945, I-356, I-485, I-129, etc.) as they relate to the proposed public charge rule; includes what factors/forms inform public-charge determinations and PRA burden reporting requirements. Intended to direct public comment and explain form applicability and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA Comment Point 1: Necessity and practical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should explain whether the requested data are needed for USCIS functions and whether they will have practical utility for adjudicating public charge determinations or other agency purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA Comment Point 2: Accuracy of burden estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should address the validity of respondent counts, time-per-response estimates, the methodology behind calculating total hours and costs, and any assumptions (e.g., respondent types) used to produce those estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA Comment Point 3: Enhance quality, utility, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments may propose edits to question wording, structure, or instructions to make collected information more useful, clearer for respondents, and more directly supportive of adjudicative needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA Comment Point 4: Minimize respondent burden / use of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology, e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should recommend ways to reduce time/cost burden (e.g., streamlined questions, electronic filing options, pre-filled data, alternative collection techniques) or identify burdensome items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge determination factors (I-944)
rubrics_metrics.description: The data collected on these forms will be used by USCIS to determine the likelihood of a declarant becoming a public charge based on the factors regarding health; family status; assets, resource, and financial status; and education and skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form I-944 is described as 'the primary basis of the public charge determination' and standardizes evaluation metrics so adjudicators can assess self-sufficiency; commenters should consider whether the form captures these factors adequately and how items map to adjudicative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Factor / medical exam (I-693)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-693 is used to report results of a medical examination to USCIS. The I-693 is used as part of the Health Factor to identify medical conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicability notes: generally required for adjustment of status applicants; nonimmigrants seeking change/extension of status generally not required. Comments can address whether the medical information collected is necessary, sufficient, or privacy-sensitive for public-charge analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Support as a public charge factor (I-864 series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement/contract provided by a sponsor to show that the sponsor has adequate financial resources to support the alien. The Affidavit of Support when required is a factor in the public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms I-864, I-864A, and I-864EZ are used to standardize evaluation of a sponsor's ability to support a sponsored immigrant; commenters may address required fields, enforcement implications, and interaction with public-charge adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-864A household member contract and liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-864A is a contract between the sponsor and the sponsor’s household members. It is only required if the sponsor used income of his or her household members to reach the required 125 percent of the FPG. The contract holds these household members jointly and severally liable for the support of the sponsored immigrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is relevant to enforcement and to how household income is counted; comments can address fairness, notice, and burden implications for household members.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-864EZ simplified sponsor form
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-864EZ: USCIS uses Form I-864EZ in exactly the same way as Form I-864; however, USCIS collects less information from the sponsors as less information is needed from those who qualify in order to make a thorough adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This represents a reduced-information path for qualifying sponsors; commenters can evaluate whether the reduced data are sufficient for public-charge assessment and whether eligibility criteria for I-864EZ are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: I-864W exemption criteria (discontinued instrument)
rubrics_metrics.description: I-864W — Certain classes of immigrants are exempt from the Form I-864 or Form I-864EZ requirement and therefore must file Form I-864W instead. (Discontinued – information incorporated into Form I-485). Conditions listed: 1. The sponsor is the person who filed or is filing Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative, for a relative being sponsored; 2. The relative the sponsor is sponsoring is the only person listed on Form I-130; and 3. The income the sponsor is using to qualify is based entirely on your salary or pension and is shown on one or more Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Form W-2s provided by your employers or former employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though I-864W is being discontinued and information incorporated elsewhere, these three eligibility conditions show what USCIS considered qualifying for reduced requirements; commenters can address clarity and transitional handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver disclosure impact (I-912)
rubrics_metrics.description: Update – provides warning that a request for a fee waiver may be a factor in the public charge determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS edits to I-912 make clear that an approved fee waiver can negatively impact eligibility for an immigration benefit subject to the public charge inadmissibility determination; commenters should assess whether this notice is adequate and its potential chilling effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public charge bond as remedial mechanism (I-945)
rubrics_metrics.description: For aliens inadmissible solely based on public charge and who are permitted to have a bond posted on his or her behalf ... This form is the bond contract between USCIS and the obligor. For aliens inadmissible solely based on public charge ... he or she may be admitted to the United States upon the posting of a suitable and proper bond at the discretion of USCIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bond guarantees conditions (e.g., that the alien will not receive public benefits as defined). Comments can address bond terms, cost, availability of surety, and fairness of admitting someone only via bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable surety and bond funding standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An acceptable surety is generally any company listed on the Department of the Treasury’s Listing of Approved Sureties (Department Circular 570) in effect on the date the bond is requested or an individual or an entity that deposits cash or a cash equivalent, such as a cashier’s check or money order for the full value of the bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies the financial instruments/entities acceptable to secure a public-charge bond; commenters may address practical availability and cost implications for petitioners and obligors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of public charge bond grounds (I-356)
rubrics_metrics.description: The form is used to request cancellation of the public charge bond because of the alien’s naturalization, permanent departure, or death. The form is also used by the alien or the obligor to request cancellation of the public charge bond upon the fifth anniversary of the alien’s admission to the United States as a lawful permanent resident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the statutory/administrative events that permit bond cancellation; comments can address process clarity, evidentiary requirements, and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form applicability and who must file
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability to Public Charge: examples — The I-693 is used as part of the Health Factor; The Affidavit of Support when required is a factor in the public charge determination; I-944 is the primary basis of the public charge determination. Generally, adjustment of status applicants are required to submit an I-693. Nonimmigrants seeking a change or extension of status are generally not required to submit an I-693. USCIS, at its discretion, may request the applicant to file a Form I-944 to determine likelihood of receipt of public benefits in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry captures the mapping of specific forms to the public-charge analysis and discretionary requests; commenters can question scope, discretion, and notice to applicants about when forms will be requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA burden disclosure elements (what must be reported)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, agencies must submit to OMB any reporting requirements inherent in a rule, including: Type of Information Collection; Title; Agency form number/component; Affected public and brief abstract; Estimate of total number of respondents and average time to respond; Estimate of total public burden (hours); Estimate of total public burden (cost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document provides example numeric estimates for many forms (e.g., respondents and hour burdens for I-944, I-485, I-864 series, I-129, etc.). Commenters should evaluate these specific estimates and the completeness of PRA disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form design objective: standardize evaluation metrics and ensure essential information
rubrics_metrics.description: The forms serve the purpose of standardizing public charge evaluation metrics and ensure that declarants provide all essential information required for USCIS to assess self-sufficiency and adjudicate the declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit design objective for the collections; commenters may propose alternate designs to better capture self-sufficiency or reduce unnecessary data collection while preserving adjudicative needs.
